description: Return the lexical parent of each supplied path string on the tested Linux implementation.

interface.semantic_input: Ordered path strings using POSIX separators.
interface.semantic_output: One parent string per input. A bare relative filename has an empty parent, while ./file has parent dot.

dependencies: C++17 standard library and filesystem support
resources: Allocates the output vector and constructs path objects. Peak memory and input-size limits are unmeasured.

preconditions.detail: The function takes an in-memory vector of strings. It applies lexical decomposition without looking up a filesystem entry.

postconditions.detail: Returned one lexical parent per input in encounter order, preserving repeated results on the fixed and constructed Linux cases.

refinements.detail: Bare relative names produced the empty string. An explicit ./ prefix produced dot. A sole slash and a file directly under slash both produced slash.

effects.detail: The direct client observed unchanged input strings. File reads and destination writes in the ordinary program belong to its surrounding reader and writer.

invariants.detail: Earlier dot and dot-dot components survived, repeated separators were rendered in generic form, and a trailing slash had an empty final component in the tested cases.

mathematical_properties.detail: On the recorded finite set of constructed triples, each result vector contained the known parent, the supplied path, and the known parent again.

formal_predicates.detail: No general proof or cross-platform pathname equivalence was established.

state_protocol.detail: The interface exposes a synchronous function with no retained client object.

ownership.detail: Borrows the vector by const reference and returns a vector of owned strings by value.

upstream_usage.detail: The retained catalog example projects one parent per record, including an empty string for a bare name.

specification_question.detail: Should a bare filename have an empty parent or be displayed under dot? This binding produces an empty parent.
